title: Impact of FDA Drug Approval on Biotech Company Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Event-study methodology.  
Rationale: FDA approval is a well-defined, sharply-timed information shock. In semi-strongly efficient capital markets, any causal price effect should be impounded in returns immediately around the announcement. By comparing realised returns to a model-based counterfactual (the market model), we can treat the difference as the causal abnormal return.

Key assumptions  
• Market efficiency: In the absence of the event, expected abnormal return is zero.  
• No confounding news in the estimation/event window.  
• Stable linear relation between the stock and the market return (β constant over the sample).  
• Cross-sectional independence (or we correct standard errors for clustering at firm level).  

## 2. R Code
```r
##############################################################################
# Event Study: FDA Drug Approval and Biotech Stock Returns
#---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Read data
# 2. Compute abnormal returns with market model
# 3. Estimate and test CAR[-1,+1]
# 4. Robustness: CAR[-2,+2] and panel regression with day-dummies
##############################################################################

library(data.table)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(fixest)

#-----------------------#
# 1. Read the dataset   #
#-----------------------#
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s63_data.csv"
dt   <- fread(path)

# quick check
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(dt)))

#-------------------------------------#
# 2. Compute Abnormal Returns (AR)    #
#-------------------------------------#
# market model with alpha = 0 (beta is pre-estimated)
dt[, AR := ret - beta * mkt_ret]

#---------------------------------------------#
# 3. CAR[-1,+1] : core estimate               #
#---------------------------------------------#
event_window_core <- -1:1
car_core <- dt[event_day %in% event_window_core,
               .(CAR = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE)), 
               by = stock_id]

# Mean CAR and t-stat (two-sided)
mean_car  <- mean(car_core$CAR)
se_car    <- sd(car_core$CAR)/sqrt(nrow(car_core))
t_stat    <- mean_car / se_car
p_value   <- 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = nrow(car_core)-1, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("==========  MAIN RESULT  =================\n")
cat("Mean CAR[-1,+1] :", round(mean_car*100,2), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic     :", round(t_stat,3), "\n")
cat("p-value         :", format.pval(p_value), "\n\n")

#---------------------------------------------#
# 4. Robustness 1: CAR[-2,+2]                 #
#---------------------------------------------#
event_window_alt <- -2:2
car_alt <- dt[event_day %in% event_window_alt,
              .(CAR = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE)), 
              by = stock_id]
mean_car_alt <- mean(car_alt$CAR)
se_car_alt   <- sd(car_alt$CAR)/sqrt(nrow(car_alt))
t_alt        <- mean_car_alt / se_car_alt
cat("Robustness – Mean CAR[-2,+2]:", round(mean_car_alt*100,2), "% | t =", round(t_alt,3), "\n\n")

#----------------------------------------------------------#
# 5. Robustness 2: Panel regression with day dummies       #
#----------------------------------------------------------#
# Create day dummies for a ±5-day window
window <- -5:5
for (d in window) dt[, paste0("D", d) := as.integer(event_day == d)]

# Fixed-effects regression of AR on day dummies (firm clustered SE)
fmla <- as.formula(paste("AR ~", paste(paste0("D", window), collapse = " + ")))
reg  <- feols(fmla, data = dt, cluster = "stock_id")

cat("Regression-based event profile (AR coefficients):\n")
print(etable(reg, keep = paste0("^D"), se.below = TRUE, digits = 3))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. FDA approval is good news, so abnormal returns should jump upward.  
Magnitude: Typical biotech announcement effects are sizeable—around +6 % to +10 % over a (-1,+1) window. Given the sample (60 firms) and historical evidence, I expect an average CAR of roughly +7 % (≈ 0.07 in decimal returns) with a t-stat near 3, indicating statistical significance.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the timing of FDA drug approval announcements as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: FDA drug approvals lead to a positive change in biotech companies' CAR.
